description: This profile represents network behavior that deviates significantly from the established normal baseline but does not map mathematically to any known attack signatures in the database. This classification serves as a critical early warning system for potential zero-day exploits, novel evasion techniques, or severe internal misconfigurations that require immediate manual threat hunting.

patterns.description: Anomalies triggered by the machine learning model's outlier detection algorithms rather than specific rules.

features.name: High Feature Outlier Score
features.description: The traffic flow exhibits a high anomaly score or reconstruction error, indicating it is statistically improbable based on the normal training data. The specific SHAP contributors will vary wildly depending on the nature of the novelty.

features.name: Unprecedented Traffic Volume/Density
features.description: A sudden, massive spike in traffic to a service that normally sees low utilization, or conversely, a complete drop in traffic from a highly active service, breaking historical time-series baselines.

patterns.description: Traffic that violates standard RFC protocols or normal operational behaviors.

features.name: Atypical Protocol/Port Combinations
features.description: Services communicating over non-standard or unexpected ports (e.g., SSH traffic over port 443, or database queries leaving the external firewall), suggesting tunneling or evasion.

features.name: Unconventional TCP/IP Flag Configurations
features.description: Packets arriving with illegal, malformed, or highly unusual combinations of TCP flags (like SYN/FIN/RST combinations) designed to confuse network inspection appliances.

patterns.category: Context and False Positives (Root Cause Analysis)
patterns.description: Common benign events that trigger zero-day or outlier alerts.

features.name: Infrastructure Evolution (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: New software deployments, massive internal system backups, architecture migrations, or unexpectedly popular new services will naturally break old baselines and appear as massive statistical anomalies until the model is retrained.

features.name: Hardware/Routing Failures
features.description: A dying switch, a misconfigured router causing broadcast storms, or a severe network loop can generate highly anomalous, chaotic traffic patterns that mimic a denial-of-service attack.
